result.summary: Return structured JSON-RPC error objects for requests rejected by -rpcwhitelist instead of an empty HTTP 403 response. Introduce RPC_METHOD_NOT_PERMITTED (-38) for denied methods (HTTP 200 for JSON-RPC 2.0, HTTP 403 for 1.x) and RPC_REQUEST_NOT_EXECUTED (-39) for remaining unexecuted calls in a rejected batch. Reformat rejected batch responses to return HTTP 200 with an array of individual errors per request.
result.problem: Requests refused by -rpcwhitelist currently return an empty HTTP 403 response, showing up as a generic transport error rather than a JSON-RPC error. This violates the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification implemented in #27101, breaks bitcoin-cli over HTTP (showing only "server returned HTTP error 403"), and causes bitcoin-cli -ipcconnect to fail with cryptic JSON parsing errors because IPC carries only the body without HTTP status codes.
evidence: Author description notes an empty body breaks IPC clients: 'bitcoin-cli -ipcconnect receives only the response body, so a refused call prints a JSON type error instead of a permission error, as described in a private security review (https://ipcbugs.ofsky.org/audits/ar-56/)'.
Commit e36e35b87c notes that returning HTTP 403 for JSON-RPC 2.0 errors directly contradicts JSONErrorReply() and doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md introduced in #27101.
result.scope_notes: Modifies RPC whitelist handling in httprpc.cpp and adds error codes to protocol.h; diff was omitted from the prompt.
result.card: This PR updates -rpcwhitelist refusals to return structured JSON-RPC error objects instead of empty HTTP 403 replies. Currently, -rpcwhitelist rejections cause generic HTTP 403 errors and crash bitcoin-cli -ipcconnect with JSON decoding errors because IPC does not receive HTTP status codes. It introduces RPC_METHOD_NOT_PERMITTED (-38) and RPC_REQUEST_NOT_EXECUTED (-39), returning HTTP 200 with an error object for JSON-RPC 2.0 requests and batch requests in alignment with the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification. The issue was discovered during a security review of the IPC interface.

risk.why: Changing the HTTP status code from 403 to 200 for JSON-RPC 2.0 and batch whitelist denials could break automated RPC clients that rely strictly on HTTP status codes rather than parsing error response bodies.
